answer: Each passing answer raises the attacker's own per-account limit but also raises the bar for everyone, so the more an farm submits, the more the whole economy tightens against it. This is why the network can stay open without a central gatekeeper: the economics of reputation do the filtering that a trusted authority otherwise would.. It is effective because voting power is weighted by verifiable work over time, so a fresh flood of accounts cannot manufacture a decisive vote. Consider a tide as the anchor of the cost.
